outcome: No new Wilson prime, search extension, or theoretical progress on the infinitude question was found since 26 January 2024; only three Wilson primes (5, 13, 563) remain known, and the question is exactly as open as it was in the frozen revision.
summary: The question is whether there are infinitely many Wilson primes (primes p such that (p-1)! ≡ -1 mod p^2). Only three are known (5, 13, 563), and the last major search (Costa, Gerbicz, and Harvey, 2013/2014, arXiv:1209.3436) ruled out any further Wilson primes below 2×10^13 — a result that predates the frozen revision and would in any case be an `open_stale`-style search record, not a resolution of the infinitude question, per the rule that existence/infinitude questions move only on an answer, not on a larger search bound. I checked the Wikipedia Wilson prime article, MathWorld, AoPS wiki, and OEIS sequences A007540 (the Wilson primes themselves) and A002068 (Wilson quotients) for any update, and ran targeted searches for new Wilson prime discoveries, extended search bounds, PrimeGrid/Ibercivis/GIMPS search activity, and any 2024-2026 arXiv work on the conjecture. The only post-January-2024 paper I found that touches Wilson quotients at all is Bernd C. Kellner's 'Wilson's theorem modulo higher prime powers I: Fermat and Wilson quotients' (arXiv:2509.05235, submitted 5 September 2025) and its companion part II (arXiv:2509.05402). I opened the abstract/metadata directly: it proves supercongruences describing Wilson's theorem and the Wilson quotient modulo higher prime powers using Bell polynomials and Fermat quotient power sums — a purely theoretical, structural result about congruence identities, not a search extension, a new Wilson prime, or any statement bearing on whether infinitely many Wilson primes exist. Under §3.1 this is a related result (adjacent theory about Wilson quotients generally) rather than a case of the stated infinitude question, so it does not move the needle on this bullet. No AI system is mentioned in this paper or anywhere else I found related to Wilson primes. I found no evidence of any distributed-computing search (PrimeGrid, GIMPS, Ibercivis) being run or extended after January 2024 specifically targeting Wilson primes. The record is therefore `open` with `no_change_found` true, matching the triage's `none` verdict.
competing_reading: One could argue the Kellner papers constitute 'progress' in a loose sense because they advance general theory around Wilson quotients that could eventually be useful to an infinitude proof or a more efficient search algorithm. But they contain no new bound, no new prime, and no argument bearing on infinitude, so under the scope rule (§3.1: a case restricts the question, a variant changes it) this is best read as adjacent background theory, not a change to this bullet.
what_would_settle_it: A new Wilson prime found beyond 5, 13, 563; a proof (or disproof) of infinitude; or, at minimum, a published extension of the search bound beyond 2×10^13 that explicitly targets Wilson primes.
